questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had visited Berlin a few times before and really liked the city. Also, I have friends who had lived in Berlin and studied at the FU, who recommended it

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy to find information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved emails with information about fx courses and there was two orientation days

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to find accommodation quite quickly. Many Danes have apartments in Berlin that they rent out, so I would look for accommodation through Facebook groups like "Danskere i Berlin" - that´s how I found my room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I know that other exchange students found it more difficult to find accommodation, and some needed to find new accommodation, while they were in Berlin, because of short-term leases (or bad conditions in the dormitories). But I didn´t meet any Danes who had had trouble finding accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some exchange students live at the dormitories that are offered by the university, which seemed very nice because of the community with the other students and cheap rent, but the conditions in the rooms are not the best and you live far away, so I would recommend looking for accommodation yourself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to register both at Campus Management and write to the professors if they had a spot available in their seminars.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information sent out from the university and information at the orientation day

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got a spot in all the seminars that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At Campus Management it is not first come, first serve. However, I could not register for all the courses I wanted there, so I had to write to the professors to get a spot in their seminar - in these cases in the popular courses it´s a good idea to write as quickly as possible to the professors, because otherwise you might not get a spot. Another important thing to know is that you can reregister for courses in the first two weeks, so you are able to “shop” around between the seminars and then reregister based on which ones you find most interesting

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of the courses appropriate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At the sociology program at Freie, it´s small seminars (max 18 students) and in most seminars it is discussion based, so the professors expect you to have read the literature and participate in the discussions. Because it is active participation, you have to be present in 85% of the seminar and hand in questions every week, do presentations or something like that depending on the seminar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Emotions and Social Class (seminar)
Mixed Methods Approaches to Migration and Health Inequalities (seminar)
Religion and Migration (seminar)
Contested Intimacies: Understanding (Non-)Monogamy (seminar)
Globalization of Science: A Gender Perspective (seminar)
Cultural Differences and Similarities (lecture)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the seminars, as I found them all interesting and you learn a lot, because you have to participate and discuss the themes. The lecture was interesting as well and the workload was quite small compared to the seminars, but I definitely feel like I learned more in the seminars

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn´t encounter any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices were what I expected, which was that it is cheaper to go out to dinner, bars, museums (almost all are free when you are a student) and so on than in Copenhagen, which made it possible to explore the city more, without being too concerned about your expenses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All different kinds of offers such as UniSport which had all sorts of sport offers for students, FU campus run/summer party

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You had to be quick to sign up for some of the sports courses in UniSport, so I didn´t participate in that, but the FU campus run/summer party was nice

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just explore the city, all the different neighborhoods, the history, go to musems, bars, flea markets, the lakes, hang out in the parks, go to Potsdam or other cities in Germany (which is free to travel to with the Semesterticket)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy to adjust, as Berlin has a lot of things in common with Copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn´t find anything particularly challenging, other than just adjusting to living away from home

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated that Berlin is very multicultural and has a lot of history

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Attend a German vorkurs at the language center at FU before the semester begins, both to learn the language, extend your stay and to get a social circle – the vorkurs was especially useful for the latter reason
2. Take the seminars rather than the lectures
3. Remember to not only focus on studying, but also enjoy and explore the city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To study at a university in another country, living outside of Denmark and meet a lot of interesting people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was being away from friends and family back home, but luckily Berlin is not that far away

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
